note: The fuzzer input starts with a UTF-32 big-endian BOM and contains an ASE signature so the memory import selects a text importer.
With no useful extension, Assimp uses signature-based detection on the raw memory stream.
The ASE token embedded after the BOM selects the ASE importer.
The selected text importer copies the input into a vector and calls common text conversion.
The vector reserves one extra byte beyond the file size for a later terminating zero.
The vector's logical size remains exactly the file length before conversion.
The BOM-prefixed buffer is passed to UTF conversion before the reserved terminator byte is added.
The first four bytes satisfy the UTF-32 big-endian BOM check.
The loop treats the address of the final byte as an inclusive uint32_t element boundary, so a non-multiple-of-four file length permits a partial final uint32_t access beyond vector size.
The final byteswap reads a 32-bit word beginning at the last byte group and crosses beyond the vector's valid elements, producing the ASan container-overflow read.
